::: {.ter-status}
Planned pathway
:::

This section intentionally describes future scope rather than presenting untested machine lessons as complete curriculum.

## Proposed learning sequence

- CNC router and CNC mill capabilities and limits;
- machine coordinates, work coordinates, and zero/reference choices;
- secure workholding and clearance planning;
- end-mill geometry and tool selection;
- CAM setup, pockets, profiles, drilling, and toolpath order;
- feeds, speeds, chip formation, and machine/material-specific evidence;
- simulation, dry-run practices, verification, inspection, and revision.

Future lessons will depend on the available machine, tooling, materials, guarding, dust or chip control, supervision, and local safe-operating procedures.

::: {.ter-curriculum-relevance}
**Ontario curriculum relevance:** Expected strongest fit with **TMJ Manufacturing Technology**, **TDJ Technological Design**, and **TCJ Construction Technology**, including relevant senior courses and emphasis areas in CAM, machining, mechanical engineering, and manufacturing. Exact mapping will follow the completed lessons.

Potential senior contexts include **TMJ3M/TMJ4M**, **TMJ3C/TMJ4C**, **TMJ3E/TMJ4E**, **TDJ3M/TDJ4M**, and **TDJ3O/TDJ4O**. These are scope notes, not claims that an unfinished lesson satisfies every course.
:::

For currently supported digital fabrication, use [Laser Cutting & 2D Fabrication](../03-laser-cutting/index.qmd) or [3D Printing](../04-3d-printing/index.qmd).
